added_lines: all saint. ‘the ultimate object of veneration of the saints is the glory of god and the sanctification of man by conforming one’s life fully to the divine will and by imitating the virtue of those who were pre-eminent disciples of the lord. catechises and other forms of doctrinal instruction should therefore make known to the faithful that our relationship with the saints must be seen in the light of the faith and should not obscure the “cultus latriae due to god the father through christ in the holy spirit, but intensify it ” november – why bother having a funeral mass? why not just go straight to the cemetery and leave out the funeral mass? in times gone by every catholic who died automatically came to the church for their funeral. in the recent times some families bypass the church and do not bring their dead to the church for the requiem or funeral mass. instead they go straight to the cemetery or crematorium. in doing so they leave jesus out. they forget that we are not merely individuals, we are part of a community of friends of jesus called the church. it is sad to see people who loved the mass and came to mass regularly not being brought to the church and giving their friends and fellow christians in the parish a chance to mark their passing with the greatest gift god has given us, the mass. why is it important to have a funeral mass? every catholic is baptized into god’s holy trinity, uniting themselves with jesus and his church. we are baptized into the death and resurrection of jesus from the dead because jesus has conquered death and opened for us the way to eternal life. so it does not make sense to leave jesus out of the equation. jesus is the whole reason for baptism, and especially for the mass. we expect to meet jesus when we die. the funeral mass is the heart of our funeral – jesus gave us the mass at the last supper just before he died on the cross. the mass only makes sense because jesus conquered death and evil by rising from the dead on easter sunday. remember the acclamation at the solemn consecration of the mass “christ has died, christ is risen, christ will come again ”. in the funeral mass we offer our dead to the father as jesus did for us on the cross. the funeral mass asks god to admit the dead catholic to the paschal fullness of the table of the kingdom. through baptism we become part of god’s family – the parish community. it is by the mass and holy communion that the community of the faithful, especially the family of the deceased, learn to live in communion with the one who "has fallen asleep in the lord," by communicating in the body of christ of which he is a living member and, then, by praying for him and with him. for christians to forget about the church funeral for the dead is to leave out the main player, jesus christ, who is our saviour. the greatest act of love you can do for your loved one who dies is to give them the gift of a catholic funeral with the complete rites of the church in accord with god’s wish for each and every member of his church when they die. saturday 31st october 6.30pm tom & rosaleen feely (anniv) grainne long (anniv) sunday 1st november 11.30am mary o’reilly (month’s mind) adele kelly (month’s mind) denis (dinnie) bullman (7th anniv) entrance hymn: ‘christ be near at either hand’ christ be near at either hand, christ behind, before me stand, christ with me wheree’er i go, christ around, above below. christ be in my heart and mind, christ within my soul enshrined, christ control my wayward heart; christ abide and ne’er depart. christ my life and only way, christ my lantern night and day; christ be my unchanging friend, guide and shepherd to the end. recessional hymn here i am lord i, the lord of sea and sky, i have heard my people cry, all who dwell in dark and sin, my hand will save. i who made the stars of night, i will make their darkness bright. who will bear my light to them? whom shall i send? here i am lord, is it i lord. i have heard you calling in the night. i will go lord, if you lead me. i will hold your people in my heart. i the lord of wind and flame. i will tend the poor and lame. i will set a feast for them. my hand will save. finest bread i will provide, till their hearts be satisfied. i will live my life to them whom shall i send? r parish of sts. mary & peter, arklow with david’s johnstown all
